{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the bottom line of the fish from the belly's low point through the crossing out to the tail tip, which is the part of the outline that completes the tail and gives the fish its recognisable silhouette. I joined it onto Omar's last domino so the run stayed connected. The final chain carried through about 121 of 124 standing dominoes, and the picture reads clearly as a fish.

Execution: I took over the bottom line at the belly, laid it in short builds of 4 to 5 dominoes, and carried it through the crossing, where two lines meet at a gentle angle. I then inspected the crossing and the bunched section before it to confirm the chain carried through. I kept my hands off the table after that to avoid bumping the work.

Collaboration: I coordinated the handover with Omar on the bottom line, so we did not both build the same stretch and the join was clean. I told the table what I was doing and checked in with Jack and Sofia about the tail. I agreed to leave the finished fish alone rather than make unnecessary changes.

Leadership: I set out clear divisions of the bottom line and the tail, and I said openly when the tail was a part of the two lines and needed no separate build. I kept the table focused on a simple outcome: a connected run, no late changes, and no bumps before the push. Sofia's design and the team's work made the result possible, and my share was the bottom-line tail and the crossing join.", "my_share_percent": 30}
